recall.define: Using the protocol lab representations, define typestate, staged builder completeness, a session transition, hierarchical-state least common ancestor, orthogonal region, run-to-completion and a driver capability.
recall.distinguish: Compare nominal C wrappers, runtime state admission and language-enforced consuming transitions. Explain why copying a wrapper or retaining a raw device pointer can invalidate a stronger typestate claim.
recall.apply: Inject an interrupted driver transition while an orthogonal state region has a queued event. Derive rollback ownership and event order, then explain which invalid calls need diagnostics and which need runtime rejection.
